$comment: Guidefold landing redesign. Direction only. The writer implements; this file never edits ui/src.
modeRationale: Owner verdict: the page carries far too much information and explains it in an over-complicated way. Structure, motion and component set are replaced. All protected content (waitlist form and its flows, privacy answer, pricing facts, availability statements, GitHub and /docs links, the YouTube demo) is carried over verbatim in substance. This is an overhaul with content preserved, not a greenfield rewrite and not a preserve pass.
visualThesis: A survey chart of a folded paper map, on graphite. One continuous cinematic field runs behind the whole page: a topographic contour plane and a dashed survey grid that drift as you scroll, with the hero's ambient loop at the top of it. The page itself is a quiet reading surface laid on that field: graphite ground, stone and ivory type, teal for system state, orange for the one place a human decides. Backgrounds move; text never does. Every interface transition is a shadcn-style 150-200ms fade or slide that confirms an action and then gets out of the way. The page answers one question at a time, in the order WHY, HOW, VALUE, and then asks for the email.

DESIGN_VARIANCE.label: Balanced / Modern
DESIGN_VARIANCE.evidence: Audience is platform teams, tech leads and developers evaluating a Git-native instruction tool (docs/PRODUCT-PIVOT.md §1: 'Pierwszy klient to platform team albo tech lead'). ui-ux-pro-max returned category 'Developer Tool / IDE' at variance 4. A higher variance conflicts with the owner's restraint verdict; a lower one loses the one piece of art direction the product actually owns (the folded-map material world).

MOTION_INTENSITY.label: Restrained
MOTION_INTENSITY.evidence: Owner: current animations are 'wrong and not in the style of shadcn components'. One ambient background loop plus data-state driven UI transitions only. No scroll-jacking, no scrubbed film, no per-word entrance, no beams, no shine sweeps, no autoplaying demo timelines. Existing tokens already sit in this range (--duration:120ms, --duration-menu:180ms, --duration-drawer:240ms).

VISUAL_DENSITY.label: Open
VISUAL_DENSITY.evidence: The single owner instruction is 'far too much information'. The current page ships a 3D pyramid scene, a schema flow canvas, two autoplaying feature demos, a workbench, a film figure and a four-question FAQ. The redesign keeps seven sections and one interactive panel. ui-ux-pro-max suggested density 4 with a Bento grid; rejected, see uiUxProMaxEvidence.

rules: One h1 on the page. Section headings are h2. The FAQ triggers stay h3 inside the collapsible, as today.
Heading weight --weight-semibold, body --weight-normal. Do not use --weight-bold on display type at this size.
All-caps eyebrow labels use --tracking-label .14em at --font-size-small and are optional; a section is allowed to have no eyebrow.

color.decision: The existing token palette is authoritative. Do not introduce a second palette. The ui-ux-pro-max colour set (#22C55E / #0F172A / #1E293B) is rejected.

color.contrastTargets: Body text on --graphite-900 >= 4.5:1. Hero headline over video >= 7:1 measured against the brightest frame of the loop inside the copy-safe field, enforced by the scrim underlay, not by luck.

material.decision: Flat graphite surfaces separated by 1px lines and the existing inset highlight shadows. Paper and stone appear only as photographic or video material, never as a CSS texture on a UI panel.

heroMediaDecision.decision: The hero is the generated ambient loop (hero-keyframe still -> hero-loop.mp4). guidefold-intro.mp4 is NOT the hero background; it is the HOW section's mechanism figure, played once on entering view and held on its last frame.
heroMediaDecision.evidence: Frames extracted from guidefold-intro.mp4 at 0s, 2s and 5s (ffmpeg, this session). At the resolved frame the isometric G mark occupies approximately x 35% to 65% and y 16% to 80% of the 1920x1080 frame, dead centre, with the orange route and its arrow terminating near x 63%, y 47%. The empty dark field to the left of the mark is only ~33% of the frame wide. A hero with a 55% copy-safe field on the left cannot be cut from that framing without translating the video ~14% to the right, which pushes the route arrow toward the frame edge and off the visible box entirely at 390x844. The clip is also a resolved shot, not a loop; archetypes.md forbids pretending a resolved shot loops.
heroMediaDecision.whyHOWisTheRightPlacement: The clip literally animates the product's mechanism: a flat folded strip unfolds into the mark, then a route with two waypoints draws itself from source to destination. That is the HOW sentence in pictures. In a bounded 16:9 panel beside the mechanism copy, its centred composition is correct rather than a problem, contrast is trivially satisfied with no scrim, and the mobile stack is natural.
heroMediaDecision.ifTheOwnerOverrides: If the owner insists the intro opens the hero, the single change is: hero archetype becomes 'Bottom-anchored product composition', the hero copy-safe field moves from 'left 55%' to 'bottom 40%', hero-keyframe is regenerated with the focal fold upper-centre instead of right-of-centre, and the intro plays once at full bleed then cross-fades over 400ms into hero-loop at its held last frame. Nothing else in this brief changes. Do not ship the left-copy hero with the intro clip behind it; the frame measurements above say it will not fit.

motionGrammar.primaryIdea: One continuous cinematic field behind the page. It drifts with scroll and carries the hero's ambient loop at the top. Everything in front of it is either static text or a shadcn state change. Backgrounds move; text never does.

layers.ambient: Hero video loop only. Owned by the media element, not by React state. Paused when hidden, off-screen, reduced-motion or Save-Data.
layers.entrance: One bounded entrance on first paint: hero eyebrow, h1, lede, actions fade in with a 2px rise, 200ms --ease-out, stagger 40ms, total <= 120ms of stagger (within the 30-80ms-per-item bar). Nothing below the fold has an entrance animation.
layers.scroll: Scroll-linked, but only on background planes and one SVG route. Never on copy, never on a control, never pinned. Each section publishes a normalized in-view progress p in [0,1] as a CSS custom property --p; every scroll-driven value is a pure function of --p, which makes reverse scrolling exact by construction. Amplitudes are capped at +/-20px per layer (40px total travel), well inside the 40px ceiling. Only transform and opacity are animated. There is no scroll-jacking, no pinning, no scrub-locked video, no section that becomes unreadable at any p.
layers.ui: data-state driven: opacity 0->1 with scale .95->1 for dialogs and panels, 150-200ms --ease-out; collapsible height animation on the FAQ, 200ms; tabs indicator slide 180ms; hover 150ms colour only (gated by @media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)); press --press-scale .98; focus ring 0ms.

scrollEngine.progressFormula: p = clamp((viewportHeight - rect.top) / (viewportHeight + rect.height), 0, 1). p is 0 the instant the section's top edge reaches the bottom of the viewport and 1 the instant its bottom edge leaves the top. It is a pure function of geometry, so it is identical scrolling up and down.
scrollEngine.implementation: One module-level sampler for the whole page: a single passive scroll listener plus a single resize listener, both of which only schedule; one requestAnimationFrame that reads each registered section's cached rect and writes --p with element.style.setProperty. Sections register and unregister through one IntersectionObserver so off-screen sections cost nothing. No React state is set per frame. No component owns a listener. Cleanup cancels the frame and disconnects the observer.
scrollEngine.consumption: All movement is expressed in CSS: transform: translate3d(0, calc((var(--p) - .5) * var(--amp)), 0). --amp is per-layer and never exceeds 40px. Opacity ramps use calc() on --p with clamp().
scrollEngine.reducedMotionAndSaveData: The sampler is never started. --p is set once to .5 on every section, so every plane renders at its mid state and the page is a correct static composition. This is the same code path as JS-disabled, where the CSS default value of --p is .5.

tokensToRetire: --landing-stagger-1..5 (70/140/210/280/350ms) - stagger chain exceeds the 300ms cap at step 5
motionGrammar.cap: No animated value may exist outside that state set. No component owns its own interval timer.

conversionStory.premise: Your coding agent can read the repo, but a rule written for one service is wrong advice for the next one. README.md line 3 and 'The problem'.
conversionStory.proof: The instruction reader shows a real SKILL.md from the bundled Meridian fixture, labelled as a fixture. The recorded YouTube demo shows the workflow end to end. No invented metrics, no customer logos, no testimonial.
conversionStory.mechanism: Rules live in Git beside the code; a hook resolves the scope of the current folder, ranks what that scope can see, and hands the agent at most four short cards; the agent loads the full text of the one or two it needs. portal/content/how-it-works.md.
conversionStory.trust: Open source today, hosted planned, priced in the open. Availability and pricing statements are stated on the page rather than hidden, and the privacy answer explains exactly what happens to the email address.
conversionStory.action: Join the waitlist (primary, one field plus consent). Secondary paths: play the demo, read the docs, run the open-source quickstart on GitHub.

hero.rationale: The owner is producing a Higgsfield ambient background loop in the folded-map / stone / graphite-teal material world in parallel. The page carries the message; the loop supplies atmosphere only. This is the archetype named in direct-motion-site-prompts/resources/archetypes.md for exactly that division of labour.
hero.fallbackIfVideoNeverArrives: The hero keyframe still (/assets/landing/hero-poster.webp, generated by GPT Images 2 before the video and delivered independently of it) at full bleed with the same scrim, over the global topo and grid planes which continue to drift with scroll. If the keyframe is also missing, the hero falls back to the global topo plane on --graphite-950 with the scrim removed; the headline contrast is then trivially satisfied. No WebGL, no canvas, no CSS-generated 'ambient' substitute: the owned topo plane already supplies the atmosphere.

sectionSequence.question: What is this and why should I care, in one breath
sectionSequence.layoutFamily: A - full-bleed ambient media with a left copy-safe field
sectionSequence.content: Eyebrow (optional), h1, lede, two actions, one trust line. Nothing else. No stats row, no logo wall, no product screenshot.
sectionSequence.notes: Copy-safe field is the left 55% on desktop, full width lower-two-thirds on mobile. The workbench/LandingWorkbench is removed from the hero.

sectionSequence.question: WHY we built it
sectionSequence.layoutFamily: B - single-column editorial statement, max 60ch, no cards
sectionSequence.content: h2, then one sentence that is the whole answer, then at most two supporting sentences. No list, no icons, no diagram.
sectionSequence.notes: This section must be readable in under fifteen seconds. If it grows a third paragraph, cut it.

sectionSequence.question: HOW it works
sectionSequence.layoutFamily: C - asymmetric split: copy column plus one interactive panel
sectionSequence.content: h2, one answer sentence, the intro clip as the mechanism figure, three short mechanism beats as plain labelled lines (not a stepper, not a canvas, not a numbered walkthrough widget), the scroll-drawn route rule beneath them, one disclosure holding the integration diagram, and the simplified instruction reader panel.
components: IntroFigure (video, plays once on enter, holds last frame)
sectionSequence.notes: Keeps the id 'how-it-works' so the existing nav anchor still resolves. The reader is the only interactive element below the fold. Desktop layout: copy column left (--landing-mechanism-columns .8fr), figure column right holding the intro panel above the instruction reader. The intro clip is the one place the brand mark animates; it never appears twice on the page.

sectionSequence.question: VALUE: what a platform team, a tech lead and developers get day to day
sectionSequence.layoutFamily: D - 3-up role grid, equal cards, stacks at 720px
sectionSequence.content: h2, one answer sentence, then exactly three role blocks: platform team, rule owner / tech lead, developers. Each block is a role label, a one-line promise and one concrete detail.
sectionSequence.notes: Three because the audience has three named roles, not for rhythm. Do not add a fourth to balance the grid.

sectionSequence.question: Can I use it now, and what will it cost
sectionSequence.layoutFamily: E - inline two-statement band with a rule between them
sectionSequence.content: The two protected availability statements, plus the open-source quickstart link and the docs link.
sectionSequence.notes: Protected: 'Open source today.' and 'Paid hosting is planned.'

sectionSequence.question: How do I stay informed
sectionSequence.layoutFamily: F - split: short heading column plus the form column
sectionSequence.content: h2, one line of context, the waitlist form verbatim, including the signup note, label, placeholder, consent text, honeypot, success state and every error string.
sectionSequence.notes: Form markup, ids, aria wiring, abort/timeout behaviour and copy are protected. Restyle only.

sectionSequence.question: The things a buyer checks before giving an email
sectionSequence.layoutFamily: G - disclosure list, all closed on load
sectionSequence.content: h2 'Before you join' and the four existing questions with their answers verbatim.
sectionSequence.notes: This is the resolution of the one conflict between the owner's verdict and the preservation contract: the pricing and privacy answers are preserved word for word but are not spent in the reading order, because every panel is closed on load and the deep links still expand.

sectionSequence.question: Where else can I go
sectionSequence.content: Wordmark, one line, four link groups as today, the availability line and the Cloudfloo credit. The oversized display wordmark is kept at --landing-footer-wordmark; it is type, not motion.
sectionSequence.notes: GitHub, /docs/, #privacy and mailto links are protected.

sectionCountNote: Seven content sections plus header and footer. The owner's simplification instruction and the preservation contract together consume every slot; there is no room and no reason to pad toward eight.

states.desktop: >=1081px. Hero is a full-bleed media band, copy in the left 55%, actions inline. HOW is an asymmetric split. VALUE is 3-up. Waitlist is a 2-column split with the form row inline (--landing-form-columns).
states.tablet: 721-1080px. Hero copy drops below the media focal point but stays inside the scrim; HOW and the waitlist collapse to one column; VALUE stays 3-up until 720px if the cards keep a 32ch measure, otherwise 2-up.
states.mobile: <=720px. Hero media is cropped with object-position 70% center so the focal fold stays visible while the copy occupies the lower field; actions stack full width at --touch-height 44px; VALUE stacks; the instruction reader keeps the tabs but drops the rule sidebar; the FAQ is unchanged.
states.loading: Poster paints first with the same composition as the first video frame. The video element is only mounted after the poster has decoded and the section is in view. The instruction reader shows the existing 'Loading instruction…' role=status fallback. The form shows the existing 'Saving…' loading label on the submit button.
states.error: Video decoder error, CORS failure or a media source that never becomes ready sets mediaFailed and leaves the poster in place; the video element is removed. A missing poster hides itself via onError (the pattern already used on the hero art image) and the hero falls back to the flat ground. Form errors keep the existing role=alert messages and preserve the typed input.
states.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. No video is downloaded or played; the poster is the hero. Entrance opacity/rise removed; content is at its final state on first paint. Collapsible, dialog and tab transitions collapse to --duration-reduced 80ms opacity only, no scale, no height animation. Hover and press transforms removed. This is a complete static page, not a slower one.
states.saveData: navigator.connection.saveData === true. Identical to reduced-motion for media: poster only, no video request, no CSS ambient drift. UI transitions stay at their normal 150-200ms because they cost no bandwidth.
states.noJs: Every section renders from the base DOM. The FAQ answers, the mechanism beats, the availability statements and the footer links are present without JavaScript. The instruction reader degrades to its default tab content; the demo dialog trigger degrades to a plain link to the YouTube URL.

Scroll film / scrubbed video - explicitly out; an ambient loop must not be converted into a scrubbed film (archetypes.md 'Combination rule')

motionPromptPacket.archetypeRuling: One archetype for the page, per archetypes.md 'Combination rule'. The scroll-driven depth planes over the rest of the page are a SECONDARY MECHANIC, not a second archetype: they are one continuous background field in the same material world that never becomes a chaptered story, never pins a section, never carries required information, and never introduces a second visual thesis. 'Layered still-scene scroll story' was considered and rejected as the primary archetype because that archetype requires discrete spatial chapters with enter/hold/exit segments, and chaptered scroll narrative is precisely the over-explanation the owner is cutting.

layerOrder: L0 (back, global, fixed): --graphite-950 flat ground, always painted, so a missing asset never shows white
L1 (global, fixed): topo-plane.webp (from topographic-route-bg.png), background-size cover, background-position center, opacity .32, filter saturate(.85), drifts with page scroll, amplitude 16px
L2 (global, fixed): survey-grid.webp tiled at 512px, opacity .10, drifts with page scroll, amplitude 40px (nearer layer, larger travel)
L3 (per section, absolute): the generated section plane (plane-why / plane-how / plane-value), opacity ramped by --p, amplitude 20px. Absent in the hero, which has its own media instead.
L4 (hero only): hero-poster.webp, object-fit cover, object-position 62% 50% desktop / 74% 50% mobile
L5 (hero only): hero-loop video, same box, same object-position, opacity 0 until canplay then 1 over 240ms; never mounted on mediaFailed, reduced-motion or Save-Data

L6: scrim underlay - --landing-hero-scrim, a left-to-right graphite gradient from rgba(7,9,12,.94) at x=0 to rgba(7,9,12,.06) at x=68%; on mobile a bottom-up gradient from rgba(7,9,12,.94) at y=100% to rgba(7,9,12,.10) at y=44%. Sections below the hero use a flat rgba(12,16,20,.72) band instead of a gradient.
L7 (front): content - eyebrow, h1, lede, actions, section copy, panels, form, FAQ - plus the media pause control if the loop is playing. Nothing at L7 ever moves with scroll.

focalRegion.desktop: right 40% of the frame, vertically centred between 26% and 74% height; the folded ridge apex sits at approximately x=74%, y=46%
focalRegion.mobile: upper 46% of the frame after the 74% 50% crop; the ridge apex must remain inside the visible box at 390x844

copySafeRegion.desktop: left edge to x=55%, from y=16% to y=84%. No high-frequency detail, no specular highlight and no luminance above 22% inside this box in any frame of the loop.
copySafeRegion.mobile: full width, from y=50% to y=96%. Same luminance ceiling.

composition.typographyRelation: In front of the media, on the scrim, never behind or split around the subject. The headline never overlaps the focal object.

scrollChoreography.sharedRule: Every entry below is a pure function of that section's --p. Reverse behaviour is therefore exact and needs no separate specification. Copy layers have amplitude 0 in every section. No section is pinned or sticky. No value uses easing over scroll; the mapping is linear in --p with clamped ramps, because an eased scroll mapping feels like lag on a trackpad.

hero.layers: L1 topo -16px, L2 grid -40px, L4/L5 hero media -12px (a slight settle, so the media does not feel glued to the viewport), L6 scrim 0, L7 copy 0
hero.mapping: translateY = (p - .5) * -amp. Hero media additionally ramps opacity 1 -> .55 across p 0.55 -> 1.0 so the headline of the WHY section below is never fighting a bright plate.
hero.mobile: amplitudes halved (topo -8px, grid -20px, media -6px). The hero media box height is fixed at 68vh so the ramp cannot cause a reflow.

why.layers: plane-why L3 (amp 20px, opacity 0 -> .42 across p 0.10 -> 0.45, then hold), L1/L2 continue globally, copy 0
why.extra: A single 1px teal keyline (--survey-teal at 18% alpha) draws across the section's top edge: scaleX from .2 to 1, transform-origin left, mapped to clamp((p - .05)/.25, 0, 1). It is decoration, it carries no state, and it is invisible under reduced motion because it renders at its p=.5 value, which is scaleX 1.
why.mobile: amp 12px; the keyline is removed (it reads as a glitch at narrow widths).

how.layers: plane-how L3 (amp 20px, opacity 0 -> .38), the intro video figure, the RouteRule SVG, copy 0
how.routeRule: An inline SVG polyline in --safety-orange, 2px, following a shallow left-to-right survey route with two circular waypoints, sitting directly under the three mechanism beats. stroke-dasharray is the path length L; stroke-dashoffset = L * (1 - q) where q = clamp((p - .18) / .44, 0, 1). Each waypoint's opacity is a step of q at .38 and .78. This is the only scroll-driven element that carries a hint of meaning, and it is redundant with the text beside it, so losing it costs nothing.
how.routeRuleStaticOverride: IMPORTANT: q at the default --p of .5 evaluates to .727, i.e. a route drawn only 73% of the way, which reads as broken rather than as a resting state. The static state is therefore an EXPLICIT OVERRIDE, not a consequence of --p: under prefers-reduced-motion, under Save-Data if the sampler is disabled, and with JavaScript off, the route rule sets q = 1 (stroke-dashoffset 0, both waypoints at full opacity) so it is fully drawn. Implement this as a CSS rule inside the reduced-motion media query and as the element's default attribute value, not as arithmetic on --p. This is the one place in the page where the static state is not simply the --p = .5 evaluation, and it is called out because the writer would otherwise implement the formula literally.
how.introVideo: Not scroll-scrubbed. It plays once at normal speed when the figure first reaches 40% visibility (IntersectionObserver, threshold .4, disconnect after firing), then holds its final frame. It has no loop attribute. It is muted, playsInline, preload='none', with poster=intro-poster.webp so the resolved mark is what the user sees before and after playback. A visible 'Replay' text button re-runs it; that button is the only control.
how.mobile: plane amp 12px; the route rule keeps its full draw because it is short; the intro figure stacks above the mechanism beats at 16:9 full width.

value.layers: plane-value L3 (amp 20px, opacity 0 -> .34), three role cards, copy 0
value.cards: The three role cards do NOT animate in. They are static. Rationale: find-animation-opportunities' frequency and function gate - this is information-dense content the visitor is reading, and moving it for style hinders. The only differentiation is a 1px border that brightens from --line to --line-hover on hover, 150ms.

availabilityWaitlistQuestionsFooter.layers: global L1/L2 only; no per-section plane
availabilityWaitlistQuestionsFooter.mapping: The global planes keep drifting, which is what makes the field feel continuous rather than four decorated boxes. Nothing local moves.
availabilityWaitlistQuestionsFooter.rationale: These are the sections where the visitor is reading pricing, typing an email, or opening a legal answer. Nothing behind them may compete.

beats: entrance / on first paint, no trigger delay: eyebrow opacity 0->1 and translateY 2px->0, 200ms --ease-out, delay 0ms. Terminal state opacity 1, translateY 0. Interruption: any keyboard focus jumps the whole stack to its terminal state immediately.
entrance / actions row: same, delay 120ms. Total entrance stagger 120ms, well under the 300ms cap; total entrance duration 320ms.

mediaReady / on video canplay: video opacity 0->1, 240ms --duration-drawer --ease-out, poster stays mounted underneath and is never removed. Terminal state: video visible, poster hidden from AT (aria-hidden) but still painted.

ambient / for the life of the section: the video loops. No JS drives it. Interruption: pause on documentHidden (visibilitychange), pause when the hero leaves the viewport (IntersectionObserver, threshold 0), pause on userPaused.

mediaFailed / on error or on a stalled load beyond 8s: video element unmounted, poster remains, no message shown to the user, one console-free silent degrade. Terminal state is identical to the reduced-motion state.

ui / dialog open (demo player): backdrop opacity 0->1 180ms --duration-menu; popup opacity 0->1 and scale .95->1, 200ms --ease-out. Close is the same values reversed at 150ms. Interruption: Escape and backdrop click both close; the iframe is unmounted on close so the video stops.
ui / collapsible (FAQ): height 0 <-> --collapsible-panel-height plus opacity, 200ms --ease-out. Interruption: a second toggle mid-animation reverses from the current height, it does not restart.
ui / tabs indicator (instruction reader): transform translateX and width to the active tab, 180ms --duration-menu --ease-out. No fade of the panel content beyond 120ms opacity.
ui / hover on buttons and links: background and border colour only, 150ms. No lift, no shadow growth, no scale up.
ui / press: scale --press-scale .98, 120ms, on pointer only; keyboard activation does not scale.
motion.interruption: Resize invalidates the cached rects and recomputes --p on the next frame; it never restarts the loop, the intro or the entrance, because every value is a function of geometry rather than of elapsed time. Breakpoint crossings at 720px and 1080px reassign object-position, scrim direction and amplitudes through CSS only. Opening the demo dialog pauses the hero loop and resumes it on close. Changing prefers-reduced-motion at runtime tears the video down through the same path as mediaFailed and stops the scroll sampler, leaving --p at .5. Fast scrolling cannot desynchronise anything: there is no timeline to fall behind, only a value read from the current rect.

media.route: still-first, then image-to-video loop. Four GPT Images 2 keyframes are generated first; keyframe 1 is both the hero poster and the Seedance 2.5 start_image. The video is an enhancement layered over a page that is already complete without it.
media.existingEvidence: prototypes/industrial-surveyor/public/assets/industrial-surveyor/ - guidefold-intro.mp4 (1920x1080, 24fps, 5.042s, hevc + aac, 3.3 MB, owned, inspected this session via ffprobe and three extracted frames), topographic-route-bg.png (2048x1024, 2.5 MB, owned), survey-grid-pattern.png (1254x1254, 1.4 MB, owned), guidefold-mark.png (1024x1024, owned). Visual rules in prototypes/industrial-surveyor/DESIGN.md. The design reference board is design-explorations/guidefold-folded-map-3x3/06-industrial-surveyor.png. All Guidefold-owned; no third-party rights question. No existing asset is an aspect-correct 16:9 hero keyframe with a 55% left copy-safe field, which is what justifies generation.
media.delivery: 16:9, 1920x1080, 10s, 24fps, silent (generate_audio false, and any residual audio track is stripped at transcode), H.264 MP4 plus a VP9 WebM, target <= 3.5 MB for the MP4. The owned intro clip is delivered separately at H.264 MP4 + WebM + a last-frame WebP poster and must have its AAC track stripped.
media.fallback: Hero: /assets/landing/hero-poster.webp (keyframe 1), always served, painted first, never removed. Below it the global topo plane on --graphite-950. HOW figure: /assets/landing/intro-poster.webp, the resolved final frame, which is a complete composition on its own. Section planes: if a generated plane is missing, that section falls back to the global topo plane alone; the page is still correct.

motionPromptPacket.responsive: Real recomposition, not a scaled-down desktop. Desktop (>=1081): hero copy left inside the 55% copy-safe field, focal fold right, horizontal scrim, actions inline; HOW is copy-left / figure-right; VALUE is 3-up. Tablet (721-1080): the hero media band shortens to 62vh, the scrim becomes bottom-up, the copy sits in the lower half, actions stay inline; HOW collapses to one column with the intro figure first; VALUE stays 3-up while the cards hold a 32ch measure, otherwise 2-up. Mobile (<=720): hero media crops to object-position 74% 50% so the ridge apex stays in frame, band is 68vh, copy occupies the bottom 46%, both actions become full-width stacked controls at 44px, the pause control moves to the top-right of the media band, all scroll amplitudes are halved, the WHY keyline is removed, and the section planes drop to opacity .28 because a small viewport magnifies texture.
motionPromptPacket.reducedMotion: Complete static state. No video element is created and no video byte is requested, for either the hero loop or the intro clip. Posters are the images. The scroll sampler never starts; --p is .5 everywhere, so every plane sits at its mid position and mid opacity and the route rule is fully drawn. The entrance transforms and opacities are removed, not shortened, so the page is fully composed on first paint. Dialog, collapsible and tabs transitions reduce to an 80ms opacity change (--duration-reduced) with no scale and no height animation. Hover and press transforms are removed. No pause control is rendered, because nothing is playing. This is a page a person can read, not a slower version of the animated one.
motionPromptPacket.saveData: navigator.connection?.saveData true: identical media behaviour to reduced motion (posters only, zero video bytes). The scroll sampler DOES still run, because it costs no bandwidth and it is what makes the page feel like the product rather than a document; if the writer measures it above 1ms per frame on a mid-range Android, it is disabled here too and --p goes to .5. UI transitions are unchanged. The instruction reader still lazy-loads on interaction; the integration diagram stays behind its disclosure at loading=lazy.
acceptance: At 1440x900, 768x1024, 390x844 and 360x800, the hero headline and lede sit entirely inside the declared copy-safe field and measure >= 7:1 contrast against the brightest frame of the loop sampled inside that field.
The fold apex is visible in all four viewports; no crop removes the focal object.
The poster composition is pixel-comparable to video frame 0: same subject position, same crop, same light direction. A poster that changes the composition is a rejection.

The loop seam is not visible: play the clip through the wrap point ten times and observe no jump in subject position, no luminance step and no direction reversal. A first/last pixel diff alone is not sufficient evidence.
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce set before load, DevTools network shows zero requests for hero-loop.mp4 or .webm.
Blocking the media URL leaves a correct page: poster visible, no layout shift, no error text, CLS contribution 0.
Tab order is nav, skip link target, hero actions, section content, form, FAQ, footer, and matches the DOM order regardless of z-order.
Switching to another browser tab pauses the loop; returning resumes it. Scrolling the hero out of view pauses it.
Opening the demo dialog pauses the loop and unmounting the dialog stops the YouTube iframe.
No animation on the page exceeds 300ms except the deliberate 240ms media cross-in, and no stagger chain exceeds 120ms total.
Scroll: at every scroll position, in every section, all body text sits at >= 4.5:1 against whatever the planes render behind it at that --p. Sample p = 0, .25, .5, .75, 1 in each section.
Scroll: scrolling down to the footer and back to the top returns every plane to its exact initial transform and opacity. Any drift means a value is not a pure function of --p and is a defect.
Scroll: no layer's translateY exceeds 40px of total travel at any breakpoint, and no scroll-driven property other than transform and opacity exists on the page.
Scroll: with the page scrolled fast from top to bottom, the Performance panel shows no layout or paint entries attributable to the sampler, and the long-task count is zero.
Scroll: exactly one scroll listener and one resize listener exist on the page (verify with getEventListeners(window) in DevTools).
Intro clip: it plays once, does not loop, and its final frame equals intro-poster.webp. Scrolling past it and back does not replay it; the Replay button does.
Intro clip: no audio track is present in the delivered file (ffprobe shows no audio stream).
Reduced motion: the sampler is never installed, --p is .5 on every section, and the route rule is fully drawn on first paint.
